raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Extend HiSparse's existing shared-index group prefetch to multi-token speculative verification, including MTP, and bound the CUDA compact-gather launch as verification expands the batch.

Related: #60072. This is separate from the platform-interface PR #62592. It composes with #60103; slot-invalidation fusion, padding-mask fusion and the all-resident resolver optimization remain in that PR and are not duplicated here.

## Claims

- Eligible pure-decode verification batches can stage follower layers' historical KV on the existing group copy stream, with a separate completion event for each layer.
- Prefetch eligibility is separate from the single-token resident-write and host-mirror policy. Mixed/prefill batches keep per-layer staging.
- Compact gather launches at most 64 thread blocks. Additional rows are processed by the existing workers; batches of at most 64 rows retain their column parallelism.
- Add native payload/graph regression cases and a reusable gather benchmark. Scoped H200 serving and profiling results are reported below; no model accuracy or acceptance improvement is claimed.

## Performance results

Measured on 8 x NVIDIA H200 with GLM-5.2-FP8, TP=8, MTP=3 and the V2 model runner. Both arms were rebuilt from frozen main `a1cfd2c1b584c4ac197db9cc9ac84a6d973d39df`; the candidate adds this PR's changes at `bb84fb5e976f941e9e2b8586f79930be64408a74`. Source/native-library pairs were checked. The table uses the original PR implementation.

Runtime: Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 595.58.03; EvalScope 1.14.1 for unprofiled serving measurements.

- Workload: 65,536 input tokens, forced 4,096 or 8,192 output tokens, concurrency 32, 32 requests per case; temperature 0, ignore EOS. Frozen GSM8K-derived long prompts are a synthetic performance workload, not a natural long-reasoning accuracy evaluation. Request bodies match between arms and actual input/output lengths were audited.
- Both arms: `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla`, 32 GiB GPU KV cache per rank, 128 GiB shared host pool, `max_model_len=73728`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=32`, prefix caching disabled, seed 42; FLASHMLA_SPARSE / DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER.
- Each initial process ran a separate C32 64K/128 warmup (excluded), then 4K output, 8K output and an 8K repeat. A separate PR process restart repeated warmup -> 4K -> 8K. The restart rows reuse the original main process's corresponding first measurements; they are not additional independent main restarts.
- TPOT is the mean of per-request `(latency - TTFT) / (output_tokens - 1)`, not inter-chunk latency. TTFT includes queueing.

All arrows below are **main -> PR**. Throughput is aggregate output tokens/s; TPOT and TTFT are client means.

| Output / run | Output tok/s | Change | TPOT (ms/token) | Change | TTFT (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K, first | 487.7481 -> 494.6458 | +1.41% | 38.14 -> 37.08 | -2.78% | 107.739 -> 107.676 |
| 8K, first | 780.2473 -> 802.4179 | +2.84% | 26.80 -> 25.35 | -5.41% | 107.713 -> 107.733 |
| 8K, same-process repeat | 782.5196 -> 800.9244 | +2.35% | 26.59 -> 25.50 | -4.10% | 107.541 -> 107.610 |
| 4K, PR restart | 487.7481 -> 495.4115 | +1.57% | 38.14 -> 36.87 | -3.33% | 107.739 -> 107.992 |
| 8K, PR restart | 780.2473 -> 803.6892 | +3.00% | 26.80 -> 25.43 | -5.11% | 107.713 -> 107.901 |

The 32 GiB series completed main 96/96, first PR process 96/96 and restarted PR process 64/64 measured requests, with **zero preemptions in both arms**. Earlier 24 GiB runs had capacity-driven preemptions; increasing capacity is a separate tuning change and its gain is not attributed to this PR.

These observations support a modest benefit for this workload: 8K-output throughput +2.35% to +3.00%, mean TPOT -4.10% to -5.41%, with essentially unchanged mean TTFT. They are not confidence intervals or a general performance guarantee. Host NUMA placement was not pinned; generated continuations and MTP acceptance can differ across processes. No accuracy or acceptance-rate improvement is claimed.

### Profiling

A separate Torch-profiler diagnostic run at 24 GiB GPU KV capacity selected pure-decode steps with 26 requests / 104 verification rows: 24 main steps versus 23 PR steps, excluding one mixed-prefill PR step. Values are medians across rank-level medians, not end-to-end serving results.

| Diagnostic metric | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPU pure-decode envelope per step | 63.0585 ms | 54.8721 ms |
| Total gather duration per step | 14.9948 ms | 16.3471 ms |
| Exposed / non-overlapped gather duration | 14.9948 ms | 5.3232 ms |
| Gather overlap fraction | 0% | 67.44% |

The trace supports the intended copy/compute overlap: exposed gather time falls about 64.5%, despite total gather duration increasing. The selected GPU interval is about 13.0% shorter; **this is not a 13% end-to-end speedup**. Tokens and cache hit/miss state may differ. HiSparse traffic counters publish every 2,000 worker calls, so their per-case deltas are not used to attribute transfer-volume changes.

#### Trace timeline: before and after

![HiSparse main versus PR: actual GPU trace timelines and 20–24 ms zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhenwenqi2024/vllm/974d68aa2b97c604003a42163f3257d926f7c606/pr63801/overlap-before-after.png)

The figure is rendered from original GPU event timestamps and durations, grouping events into per-category interval unions. **Left: main. Right: main + this PR.** Orange shows HiSparse gather kernels reading mapped host KV; blue shows other GPU activity; purple is the measured time intersection of the two tracks. In the magnified main panel, gather occupies gaps between other GPU work. In the PR panel, gather runs concurrently with other kernels; the original events include sparse MLA attention, fused MoE and GEMM kernels in these overlapping intervals.

Both panels show **rank 0, 26 requests / 104 verification rows, 24 GiB GPU KV**. To select a representative example, each arm uses the pure-decode step nearest its own rank's median GPU envelope: main step 22 and PR step 21 (zero-based profiler indices). Each panel starts at its own first GPU event; the lower panels show the same relative 20–24 ms window in the separate executions.

| Metric in the displayed step | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPU envelope | 63.0919 ms | 54.8733 ms |
| Gather duration (interval union) | 15.0741 ms | 16.6993 ms |
| Gather overlapped with other GPU activity | 0 ms | 10.9321 ms |
| Gather without other GPU activity | 15.0741 ms | 5.7672 ms |
| Gather overlap fraction | 0% | 65.46% |

The gather duration itself increases in this example, while much of it executes alongside other GPU work. **65.46% is this single rank/step's overlap; 67.44% in the table above is the summary across rank-level medians.** Generated tokens and cache states can differ between executions. A time intersection is not a direct measurement of critical-path savings, and this 24 GiB diagnostic is separate from the unprofiled 32 GiB serving results.

## GSM8K accuracy and MTP acceptance

Full real-weight regression on the same 8 x H200, GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8/MTP3, V2 runner and 32 GiB KV configuration above, comparing frozen main `a1cfd2c1` with main + original PR `bb84fb5e`.

Protocol: EvalScope 1.14.1 / GSM8K adapter v1.1, standard `main/test` **all 1,319 questions**, first four training examples in fixed order, thinking enabled with `reasoning_effort=max`, temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 42, concurrency 32, `max_tokens=16384`, normal EOS, non-streaming, no retries. This is a custom greedy regression, not a reproduction of the official GLM model-card score. Dataset: `openai/grade-school-math@3101c7d5072418e28b9008a6636bde82a006892c`; test SHA256 `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. The complete request bodies and model metadata hashes matched across arms.

| Metric | Main | Main + PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unique questions / scored | 1,319 / 1,319 | 1,319 / 1,319 |
| Correct | 1,285 | 1,282 |
| Accuracy, all questions | 97.4223% | 97.1948% |
| Output-budget failures, scored zero | 14 | 8 |
| HTTP errors / missing / duplicate questions | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Accepted / proposed draft tokens | 781,084 / 910,050 | 705,864 / 831,003 |
| Speculative steps | 303,350 | 277,001 |
| True draft-token acceptance | 85.8287% | 84.9412% |
| Mean acceptance length, including bonus token | 3.5749 | 3.5482 |
| Position 1 / 2 / 3 unconditional acceptance | 94.6313% / 86.1961% / 76.6586% | 94.3011% / 85.3723% / 75.1503% |
| Preemptions | 0 | 0 |

Accuracy changed by **-0.2274 percentage points (three fewer correct answers)**: 11 main-correct answers became wrong, and eight main-wrong answers became correct. All eight gains came from baseline output-budget failures; four of the 11 losses were PR output-budget failures. Every budget failure reached 16,384 tokens with reasoning but no final answer and remained a zero in the full denominator. This single pass does not establish accuracy equivalence or isolate the cause of the differences; no accuracy improvement is claimed.

Acceptance is `sum(accepted) / sum(proposed)`; mean acceptance length is `1 + sum(accepted) / sum(steps)`. All per-request counters, histograms and three position counts reconciled exactly with isolated Prometheus deltas. The table includes the budget failures and excludes the preceding 20-question smoke runs. It does not use EvalScope's streaming-chunk acceptance estimate.

As a secondary diagnostic, excluding the union of either arm's truncated questions leaves the **same 1,300 questions** in both arms: acceptance is 83.8127% -> 83.9579%. This illustrates sensitivity of the token-weighted aggregate to generated continuation lengths; it is not the primary metric or evidence of an acceptance improvement.

Raw responses, per-question reviews/reports, request hashes, metrics snapshots, source-patch hash and native-library identities were archived and audited. The baseline was re-audited without regenerating answers or changing scores after correcting the harness's classification of scored budget failures; the initial failed audit remains preserved. The model/PR implementation and frozen generation protocol were unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Full EvalScope command</summary>

`DATASET_DIR` contains the frozen official train/test JSONL files and the local `main` split mapping; `OUT` is a fresh directory for each variant. Port 18593 is the local raw-response audit proxy forwarding to the model on 18592.

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --model GLM-5.2-FP8 --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://127.0.0.1:18593/v1 --api-key EMPTY \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-args "{\"gsm8k\":{\"dataset_id\":\"$DATASET_DIR\",\"few_shot_num\":4,\"few_shot_random\":false,\"subset_list\":[\"main\"]}}" \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0,"top_p":1,"max_tokens":16384,"seed":42,"timeout":7200,"stream":false,"n":1,"retries":0,"extra_body":{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true,"reasoning_effort":"max"}}}' \
  --eval-batch-size 32 --seed 42 --work-dir "$OUT" --no-timestamp
```

</details>

These are standard short GSM8K prompts, not inputs padded to 64K. They do not alone validate long-history offload misses or establish performance gains; the separate 64K performance and byte-level device tests above address different aspects.

## Validation

### Rebase validation (2026-10-29)

Rebased the original PR commit `bb84fb5e976` onto main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`; the updated head is `fc1fd11a1d306ab5f7b2d00e12107d3076e188af`. The only textual conflict was two tests added at the same location in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`. Both main's resident-gather stride/payload test and this PR's bounded-decode prefetch test were preserved unchanged, including their parametrization. A per-file comparison verified that all added/removed lines in the seven-file PR patch are identical to the original patch; only surrounding context changed.

- On the isolated rebased Python source, `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k 'hisparse_resident_gather_preserves_stride_and_payload or hisparse_group_prefetch_requires_bounded_decode_only'`: **10 passed, 55 deselected**. These are CPU tests run with the existing CUDA environment's import dependencies, not a rebuild or device validation of the new base.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed: Ruff check/format, mypy, typos, Markdown formatting, Buildkite keys/test tethering, SPDX/import/config checks, boolean-context/remote-code checks, filenames and Docker ignore rules. The test-tethering check used UTF-8 on Windows. The Windows clang-format launcher failed, so the exact rebased CUDA source was checked on Linux with **clang-format 21.1.2 `--style=file --dry-run --Werror csrc/hisparse_kernels.cu`**, which passed. Python syntax and `git diff --check` also passed.

The performance, profiling, device-test and GSM8K measurements reported above/below remain results for frozen main `a1cfd2c1` plus the original PR `bb84fb5e`; they have **not** been rerun on the new main base.

Linux/CUDA native builds and H200 device checks have now run:

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k hisparse`: main **45 passed**, PR **53 passed** (12 deselected each).
- Attention HiSparse selection: **53 main / 67 PR passed using out-of-tree compatibility copies** that repaired stale fixtures while preserving assertions. The unmodified baseline selection had 6 fixture failures / 47 passes; this is not a claim that the unmodified checked-in attention suite passed.
- Supplemental `validation/test_pr63801_device_stress.py`: **2 main / 2 PR passed**, eager and CUDA Graph replay, exact independent CPU byte-level golden comparisons; 656-byte rows, top-k 2048, four layers, up to 32 requests x 4 verification rows with changing active counts. PR Compute Sanitizer memcheck: **2 passed, 0 errors**.
- Supplemental `validation/test_pr63801_stream_consumption.py`: **2 main / 2 PR passed**, eager and CUDA Graph, immediate compute-stream consumption of each layer while follower prefetch proceeds, 64K history and an explicit logical-index readiness event. PR memcheck independently on GPU 0 and GPU 1: **2 passed, 0 errors on each**. These supplemental local tests are not checked-in full-model accuracy tests.

The standard reduced-model E2E suite (`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`), real-weight accuracy under long-history offload misses, repeated accuracy runs and a broader concurrency / MTP-on-off sweep remain outstanding. The completed standard GSM8K regression above and byte-level device checks do not replace these.

Previously recorded local checks: the isolated CPU harness passed 10 contract cases (stand-in runtime owner); Ruff, syntax, whitespace, markdownlint, typos, SPDX/import checks, Buildkite test tethering and isolated Python 3.11 mypy passed. LLVM 21.1.2 WASM formatting produced identical CUDA source bytes; the native Windows formatter hook was skipped because its launcher failed. These are local results, not a claim of upstream CI success.

## Details

Group prefetch already exists for single-token decode. This extends its eligibility without adding a backend support flag, stream, buffer or CPU readback. Current verification KV remains resident and is written by each layer before its attention; only historical host misses are staged early.

The compact gather previously targeted 64 blocks but launched one block per row once the row count exceeded 64. For example, 32 requests with four verification rows produced a 128-block copy grid. Workers now loop over those rows within a 64-block launch. Miss-count clamping, invalid entries, out-of-range source zeroing and padded hot-page strides keep their existing behavior. Tests cover row counts around the boundary, empty plans, payload bytes and replay with updated inputs.

The launch bound may trade dense-copy bandwidth for compute overlap, as illustrated by the diagnostic trace above. A block-count bound does not reserve particular SMs.

An open-PR search found no equivalent speculative-group-prefetch or bounded-gather change. #60103 handles separate existing launch/resolver overhead; #61263 changes residency hash probing.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, performance/accuracy analysis and preparation of this update. Human review and the remaining validation items above are still outstanding.

Hi @MatthewBonanni, thanks for investigating this.

I reviewed the changes in this PR at e664ca7, focusing on stream synchronization and buffer reuse. For our TP8/MTP3, DP1 configuration with DBO disabled, I haven’t identified a new TopK race introduced by the patch:
- The resolver waits for logical_topk_ready before reading logical TopK indices. Prefetched follower gathers consume the resulting miss plan, so they do not extend the logical TopK read lifetime.
- The resolver and gathers are ordered on the same group copy stream, and each layer’s attention waits for its own gather-completion event.
- The bounded gather grid preserves the row/column work partition without introducing additional shared state.
This is a static review, so it does not rule out a runtime race.

Could you share which TopK path/backend reproduces the issue, and whether you’ve made any further progress narrowing it down? In particular, is the issue in TopK generation, logical-to-physical conversion, or MTP index reuse? The failing configuration and symptom would help us focus the investigation.

Thanks again!

Following up on the race: it isn't TopK, and it isn't a bug in this PR. The crash is a cluster-barrier race in FlashInfer's MNNVL fused allreduce + residual + RMSNorm kernel, which vLLM's eager `fused_allreduce_rms_norm` uses by default on single-node NVSwitch at TP≥4.

**Root cause.** Since flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3385 (still on FlashInfer main), `LamportFlags::ctaArrive()` has every thread call `__cluster_barrier_arrive()`, but only warp 0 of cluster rank 0 calls `__cluster_barrier_wait()`. Before that change it was a full `cluster.sync()`. The other CTAs then run the RMSNorm cluster reduction, which writes into peer CTAs' shared memory via `cluster.map_shared_rank`, with no guarantee the peer CTA is resident. If the timing slips, that DSMEM write lands on an absent CTA:
- Xid 13 `Graphics SM Cga Exception: CTA Not Present`
- a sticky `unspecified launch failure`

**Why this PR exposes it.** The PR queues more zero-copy host-memory gathers on the HiSparse copy stream, and now does so on spec-verify batches too. Those gathers run concurrently with the fused AR-norm, and the host reads shift CTA timing enough to hit the window. Main crashes too if you add the same gathers.

**Evidence.** I used a standalone repro with no vLLM code (below). It runs the MNNVL `allreduce_fusion` in a loop while a side stream runs a trivial kernel reading random rows of host memory. TP4, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, torch 2.14.0+cu130.

| Config | H200, driver 595.71.05 (VM) | H100, driver 580.126.09 (bare metal) |
|---|---|---|
| MNNVL, side stream on | Xid 13 within seconds | Xid 13 within seconds |
| MNNVL, two-shot / PDL off / pinned memory | Xid 13 | Xid 13 (two-shot) |
| MNNVL, side stream off | no crash | no crash |
| MNNVL, side kernel reads device memory | no crash | — |
| `trtllm` backend | no crash | — |
| **MNNVL + one-line fix (below)** | — | **no crash, one-shot and two-shot** |

`compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck` on the unpatched kernel, with no side stream, reports `Potential invalid __shared__ write ... located in a block that might not have entered yet` in `oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel`. It reports nothing on the patched kernel.

**Fix (FlashInfer).** Make every thread wait after arriving, which restores the pre-#3385 synchronization:

```diff
       __cluster_barrier_arrive();
+      __cluster_barrier_wait();
       if (cluster.block_rank() == 0 && threadIdx.x < 32) {
-        __cluster_barrier_wait();
         arriveCounter(threadIdx.x);
       }
```

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/7782

Until that lands in FlashInfer, `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=trtllm` avoids the kernel; it's clean in the standalone, but I haven't confirmed it at server level. Perf numbers from my earlier runs still stand.

```python
"""vLLM-free repro: FlashInfer MNNVL fused allreduce+residual+RMSNorm on the compute
stream while a side stream runs a trivial zero-copy kernel reading random host rows.

torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 fi_repro.py <seconds> <side:on|off>
Env: BACKEND=mnnvl|trtllm, HOSTMEM=register|pinned, SRC=host|device, ONESHOT=1|0, PDL=1|0
"""

import os
import sys
import time

import flashinfer.comm as fc
from flashinfer.comm.comm_backend import TorchDistBackend
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load_inline

_SRC = r"""
#include <torch/extension.h>
#include <ATen/cuda/CUDAContext.h>
__global__ void zc_gather(const uint4* __restrict__ host, uint4* __restrict__ dst,
                          const int* __restrict__ rows, int n, int vec_per_row) {
  int warp = (blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x) / 32, lane = threadIdx.x % 32;
  int nwarps = gridDim.x * blockDim.x / 32;
  for (int i = warp; i < n; i += nwarps) {
    const uint4* src = host + (long long)rows[i] * vec_per_row;
    uint4* d = dst + (long long)i * vec_per_row;
    for (int j = lane; j < vec_per_row; j += 32) __stcg(d + j, __ldcg(src + j));
  }
}
void launch(int64_t host, torch::Tensor dst, torch::Tensor rows, int64_t row_bytes) {
  zc_gather<<<64, 512, 0, at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()>>>(
      (const uint4*)host, (uint4*)dst.data_ptr(), rows.data_ptr<int>(), rows.numel(),
      (int)(row_bytes / 16));
}
"""

secs = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 300
side_on = (sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "on") == "on"
rank, world = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]), int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
dev = torch.device("cuda", rank)
dist.init_process_group("nccl", device_id=dev)
cpu_group = dist.new_group(backend="gloo")

HIDDEN, MAX_TOK = 6144, 170
ROWS = int(os.environ.get("ROWS", "16"))
oneshot = {"1": True, "0": False}.get(os.environ.get("ONESHOT", ""))
```

detail.body:
## Overview

Extend HiSparse's existing shared-index group prefetch to multi-token speculative verification, including MTP, and bound the CUDA compact-gather launch as verification expands the batch.

Related: #60072. This is separate from the platform-interface PR #62592. It composes with #60103; slot-invalidation fusion, padding-mask fusion and the all-resident resolver optimization remain in that PR and are not duplicated here.

## Claims

- Eligible pure-decode verification batches can stage follower layers' historical KV on the existing group copy stream, with a separate completion event for each layer.
- Prefetch eligibility is separate from the single-token resident-write and host-mirror policy. Mixed/prefill batches keep per-layer staging.
- Compact gather launches at most 64 thread blocks. Additional rows are processed by the existing workers; batches of at most 64 rows retain their column parallelism.
- Add native payload/graph regression cases and a reusable gather benchmark. Scoped H200 serving and profiling results are reported below; no model accuracy or acceptance improvement is claimed.

## Performance results

Measured on 8 x NVIDIA H200 with GLM-5.2-FP8, TP=8, MTP=3 and the V2 model runner. Both arms were rebuilt from frozen main `a1cfd2c1b584c4ac197db9cc9ac84a6d973d39df`; the candidate adds this PR's changes at `bb84fb5e976f941e9e2b8586f79930be64408a74`. Source/native-library pairs were checked. The table uses the original PR implementation.

Runtime: Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 595.58.03; EvalScope 1.14.1 for unprofiled serving measurements.

- Workload: 65,536 input tokens, forced 4,096 or 8,192 output tokens, concurrency 32, 32 requests per case; temperature 0, ignore EOS. Frozen GSM8K-derived long prompts are a synthetic performance workload, not a natural long-reasoning accuracy evaluation. Request bodies match between arms and actual input/output lengths were audited.
- Both arms: `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla`, 32 GiB GPU KV cache per rank, 128 GiB shared host pool, `max_model_len=73728`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=32`, prefix caching disabled, seed 42; FLASHMLA_SPARSE / DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER.
- Each initial process ran a separate C32 64K/128 warmup (excluded), then 4K output, 8K output and an 8K repeat. A separate PR process restart repeated warmup -> 4K -> 8K. The restart rows reuse the original main process's corresponding first measurements; they are not additional independent main restarts.
- TPOT is the mean of per-request `(latency - TTFT) / (output_tokens - 1)`, not inter-chunk latency. TTFT includes queueing.

All arrows below are **main -> PR**. Throughput is aggregate output tokens/s; TPOT and TTFT are client means.

| Output / run | Output tok/s | Change | TPOT (ms/token) | Change | TTFT (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K, first | 487.7481 -> 494.6458 | +1.41% | 38.14 -> 37.08 | -2.78% | 107.739 -> 107.676 |
| 8K, first | 780.2473 -> 802.4179 | +2.84% | 26.80 -> 25.35 | -5.41% | 107.713 -> 107.733 |
| 8K, same-process repeat | 782.5196 -> 800.9244 | +2.35% | 26.59 -> 25.50 | -4.10% | 107.541 -> 107.610 |
| 4K, PR restart | 487.7481 -> 495.4115 | +1.57% | 38.14 -> 36.87 | -3.33% | 107.739 -> 107.992 |
| 8K, PR restart | 780.2473 -> 803.6892 | +3.00% | 26.80 -> 25.43 | -5.11% | 107.713 -> 107.901 |

The 32 GiB series completed main 96/96, first PR process 96/96 and restarted PR process 64/64 measured requests, with **zero preemptions in both arms**. Earlier 24 GiB runs had capacity-driven preemptions; increasing capacity is a separate tuning change and its gain is not attributed to this PR.

These observations support a modest benefit for this workload: 8K-output throughput +2.35% to +3.00%, mean TPOT -4.10% to -5.41%, with essentially unchanged mean TTFT. They are not confidence intervals or a general performance guarantee. Host NUMA placement was not pinned; generated continuations and MTP acceptance can differ across processes. No accuracy or acceptance-rate improvement is claimed.

### Profiling

A separate Torch-profiler diagnostic run at 24 GiB GPU KV capacity selected pure-decode steps with 26 requests / 104 verification rows: 24 main steps versus 23 PR steps, excluding one mixed-prefill PR step. Values are medians across rank-level medians, not end-to-end serving results.

| Diagnostic metric | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPU pure-decode envelope per step | 63.0585 ms | 54.8721 ms |
| Total gather duration per step | 14.9948 ms | 16.3471 ms |
| Exposed / non-overlapped gather duration | 14.9948 ms | 5.3232 ms |
| Gather overlap fraction | 0% | 67.44% |

The trace supports the intended copy/compute overlap: exposed gather time falls about 64.5%, despite total gather duration increasing. The selected GPU interval is about 13.0% shorter; **this is not a 13% end-to-end speedup**. Tokens and cache hit/miss state may differ. HiSparse traffic counters publish every 2,000 worker calls, so their per-case deltas are not used to attribute transfer-volume changes.

#### Trace timeline: before and after

![HiSparse main versus PR: actual GPU trace timelines and 20–24 ms zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhenwenqi2024/vllm/974d68aa2b97c604003a42163f3257d926f7c606/pr63801/overlap-before-after.png)

The figure is rendered from original GPU event timestamps and durations, grouping events into per-category interval unions. **Left: main. Right: main + this PR.** Orange shows HiSparse gather kernels reading mapped host KV; blue shows other GPU activity; purple is the measured time intersection of the two tracks. In the magnified main panel, gather occupies gaps between other GPU work. In the PR panel, gather runs concurrently with other kernels; the original events include sparse MLA attention, fused MoE and GEMM kernels in these overlapping intervals.

Both panels show **rank 0, 26 requests / 104 verification rows, 24 GiB GPU KV**. To select a representative example, each arm uses the pure-decode step nearest its own rank's median GPU envelope: main step 22 and PR step 21 (zero-based profiler indices). Each panel starts at its own first GPU event; the lower panels show the same relative 20–24 ms window in the separate executions.

| Metric in the displayed step | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPU envelope | 63.0919 ms | 54.8733 ms |
| Gather duration (interval union) | 15.0741 ms | 16.6993 ms |
| Gather overlapped with other GPU activity | 0 ms | 10.9321 ms |
| Gather without other GPU activity | 15.0741 ms | 5.7672 ms |
| Gather overlap fraction | 0% | 65.46% |

The gather duration itself increases in this example, while much of it executes alongside other GPU work. **65.46% is this single rank/step's overlap; 67.44% in the table above is the summary across rank-level medians.** Generated tokens and cache states can differ between executions. A time intersection is not a direct measurement of critical-path savings, and this 24 GiB diagnostic is separate from the unprofiled 32 GiB serving results.

## GSM8K accuracy and MTP acceptance

Full real-weight regression on the same 8 x H200, GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8/MTP3, V2 runner and 32 GiB KV configuration above, comparing frozen main `a1cfd2c1` with main + original PR `bb84fb5e`.

Protocol: EvalScope 1.14.1 / GSM8K adapter v1.1, standard `main/test` **all 1,319 questions**, first four training examples in fixed order, thinking enabled with `reasoning_effort=max`, temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 42, concurrency 32, `max_tokens=16384`, normal EOS, non-streaming, no retries. This is a custom greedy regression, not a reproduction of the official GLM model-card score. Dataset: `openai/grade-school-math@3101c7d5072418e28b9008a6636bde82a006892c`; test SHA256 `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. The complete request bodies and model metadata hashes matched across arms.

| Metric | Main | Main + PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unique questions / scored | 1,319 / 1,319 | 1,319 / 1,319 |
| Correct | 1,285 | 1,282 |
| Accuracy, all questions | 97.4223% | 97.1948% |
| Output-budget failures, scored zero | 14 | 8 |
| HTTP errors / missing / duplicate questions | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Accepted / proposed draft tokens | 781,084 / 910,050 | 705,864 / 831,003 |
| Speculative steps | 303,350 | 277,001 |
| True draft-token acceptance | 85.8287% | 84.9412% |
| Mean acceptance length, including bonus token | 3.5749 | 3.5482 |
| Position 1 / 2 / 3 unconditional acceptance | 94.6313% / 86.1961% / 76.6586% | 94.3011% / 85.3723% / 75.1503% |
| Preemptions | 0 | 0 |

Accuracy changed by **-0.2274 percentage points (three fewer correct answers)**: 11 main-correct answers became wrong, and eight main-wrong answers became correct. All eight gains came from baseline output-budget failures; four of the 11 losses were PR output-budget failures. Every budget failure reached 16,384 tokens with reasoning but no final answer and remained a zero in the full denominator. This single pass does not establish accuracy equivalence or isolate the cause of the differences; no accuracy improvement is claimed.

Acceptance is `sum(accepted) / sum(proposed)`; mean acceptance length is `1 + sum(accepted) / sum(steps)`. All per-request counters, histograms and three position counts reconciled exactly with isolated Prometheus deltas. The table includes the budget failures and excludes the preceding 20-question smoke runs. It does not use EvalScope's streaming-chunk acceptance estimate.

As a secondary diagnostic, excluding the union of either arm's truncated questions leaves the **same 1,300 questions** in both arms: acceptance is 83.8127% -> 83.9579%. This illustrates sensitivity of the token-weighted aggregate to generated continuation lengths; it is not the primary metric or evidence of an acceptance improvement.

Raw responses, per-question reviews/reports, request hashes, metrics snapshots, source-patch hash and native-library identities were archived and audited. The baseline was re-audited without regenerating answers or changing scores after correcting the harness's classification of scored budget failures; the initial failed audit remains preserved. The model/PR implementation and frozen generation protocol were unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Full EvalScope command</summary>

`DATASET_DIR` contains the frozen official train/test JSONL files and the local `main` split mapping; `OUT` is a fresh directory for each variant. Port 18593 is the local raw-response audit proxy forwarding to the model on 18592.

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --model GLM-5.2-FP8 --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://127.0.0.1:18593/v1 --api-key EMPTY \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-args "{\"gsm8k\":{\"dataset_id\":\"$DATASET_DIR\",\"few_shot_num\":4,\"few_shot_random\":false,\"subset_list\":[\"main\"]}}" \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0,"top_p":1,"max_tokens":16384,"seed":42,"timeout":7200,"stream":false,"n":1,"retries":0,"extra_body":{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true,"reasoning_effort":"max"}}}' \
  --eval-batch-size 32 --seed 42 --work-dir "$OUT" --no-timestamp
```

</details>

These are standard short GSM8K prompts, not inputs padded to 64K. They do not alone validate long-history offload misses or establish performance gains; the separate 64K performance and byte-level device tests above address different aspects.

## Validation

### Rebase validation (2026-10-29)

Rebased the original PR commit `bb84fb5e976` onto main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`; the updated head is `fc1fd11a1d306ab5f7b2d00e12107d3076e188af`. The only textual conflict was two tests added at the same location in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`. Both main's resident-gather stride/payload test and this PR's bounded-decode prefetch test were preserved unchanged, including their parametrization. A per-file comparison verified that all added/removed lines in the seven-file PR patch are identical to the original patch; only surrounding context changed.

- On the isolated rebased Python source, `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k 'hisparse_resident_gather_preserves_stride_and_payload or hisparse_group_prefetch_requires_bounded_decode_only'`: **10 passed, 55 deselected**. These are CPU tests run with the existing CUDA environment's import dependencies, not a rebuild or device validation of the new base.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed: Ruff check/format, mypy, typos, Markdown formatting, Buildkite keys/test tethering, SPDX/import/config checks, boolean-context/remote-code checks, filenames and Docker ignore rules. The test-tethering check used UTF-8 on Windows. The Windows clang-format launcher failed, so the exact rebased CUDA source was checked on Linux with **clang-format 21.1.2 `--style=file --dry-run --Werror csrc/hisparse_kernels.cu`**, which passed. Python syntax and `git diff --check` also passed.

The performance, profiling, device-test and GSM8K measurements reported above/below remain results for frozen main `a1cfd2c1` plus the original PR `bb84fb5e`; they have **not** been rerun on the new main base.

Linux/CUDA native builds and H200 device checks have now run:

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k hisparse`: main **45 passed**, PR **53 passed** (12 deselected each).
- Attention HiSparse selection: **53 main / 67 PR passed using out-of-tree compatibility copies** that repaired stale fixtures while preserving assertions. The unmodified baseline selection had 6 fixture failures / 47 passes; this is not a claim that the unmodified checked-in attention suite passed.
- Supplemental `validation/test_pr63801_device_stress.py`: **2 main / 2 PR passed**, eager and CUDA Graph replay, exact independent CPU byte-level golden comparisons; 656-byte rows, top-k 2048, four layers, up to 32 requests x 4 verification rows with changing active counts. PR Compute Sanitizer memcheck: **2 passed, 0 errors**.
- Supplemental `validation/test_pr63801_stream_consumption.py`: **2 main / 2 PR passed**, eager and CUDA Graph, immediate compute-stream consumption of each layer while follower prefetch proceeds, 64K history and an explicit logical-index readiness event. PR memcheck independently on GPU 0 and GPU 1: **2 passed, 0 errors on each**. These supplemental local tests are not checked-in full-model accuracy tests.

The standard reduced-model E2E suite (`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`), real-weight accuracy under long-history offload misses, repeated accuracy runs and a broader concurrency / MTP-on-off sweep remain outstanding. The completed standard GSM8K regression above and byte-level device checks do not replace these.

Previously recorded local checks: the isolated CPU harness passed 10 contract cases (stand-in runtime owner); Ruff, syntax, whitespace, markdownlint, typos, SPDX/import checks, Buildkite test tethering and isolated Python 3.11 mypy passed. LLVM 21.1.2 WASM formatting produced identical CUDA source bytes; the native Windows formatter hook was skipped because its launcher failed. These are local results, not a claim of upstream CI success.

## Details

Group prefetch already exists for single-token decode. This extends its eligibility without adding a backend support flag, stream, buffer or CPU readback. Current verification KV remains resident and is written by each layer before its attention; only historical host misses are staged early.

The compact gather previously targeted 64 blocks but launched one block per row once the row count exceeded 64. For example, 32 requests with four verification rows produced a 128-block copy grid. Workers now loop over those rows within a 64-block launch. Miss-count clamping, invalid entries, out-of-range source zeroing and padded hot-page strides keep their existing behavior. Tests cover row counts around the boundary, empty plans, payload bytes and replay with updated inputs.

The launch bound may trade dense-copy bandwidth for compute overlap, as illustrated by the diagnostic trace above. A block-count bound does not reserve particular SMs.

An open-PR search found no equivalent speculative-group-prefetch or bounded-gather change. #60103 handles separate existing launch/resolver overhead; #61263 changes residency hash probing.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, performance/accuracy analysis and preparation of this update. Human review and the remaining validation items above are still outstanding.

+"""Compare HiSparse compact gather across builds, including sparse MTP plans."""
+
+import json
+import statistics

+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv
+
+
+def benchmark(args, num_rows: int) -> dict:
+    block_size = 64
+    host_rows = num_rows * args.top_k
+    host = torch.ones((host_rows, args.row_bytes), dtype=torch.uint8, pin_memory=True)
+    hot = torch.empty(
+        (cdiv(host_rows, block_size), block_size, args.row_bytes),
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    rows = torch.arange(host_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").view(
+        num_rows, args.top_k
+    )
+    counts = torch.zeros(num_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    misses = int(args.top_k * args.miss_ratio)
+    counts[:: args.active_every] = misses
+
+    def run():
+        torch.ops._C_cache_ops.hisparse_gather_compact(host, hot, rows, rows, counts)
+
+    samples = [
+        triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(run, rep=args.rep_ms)
+        for _ in range(args.repeats)
+    ]
+    median_ms = statistics.median(samples)
+    bytes_copied = cdiv(num_rows, args.active_every) * misses * args.row_bytes
+    return {
+        "rows": num_rows,
+        "top_k": args.top_k,
+        "row_bytes": args.row_bytes,
+        "miss_ratio": args.miss_ratio,
+        "active_every": args.active_every,
+        "latency_us": [ms * 1000 for ms in samples],
+        "median_us": median_ms * 1000,
+        "host_to_device_GB_s": bytes_copied / median_ms / 1e6,
+    }
+
+

+    parser = FlexibleArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--rows", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 8, 32, 64, 65, 128, 256]
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=2048)
+    parser.add_argument("--row-bytes", type=int, default=576)
+    parser.add_argument("--miss-ratio", type=float, default=1.0)
+    parser.add_argument("--active-every", type=int, default=1)
+    parser.add_argument("--rep-ms", type=int, default=100)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=5)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if (

+            args.top_k,
+            args.row_bytes,
+            args.active_every,
+            args.rep_ms,
+            args.repeats,

+        <= 0

+        or not 0 <= args.miss_ratio <= 1
+    ):

Following up on the race: it isn't TopK, and it isn't a bug in this PR. The crash is a cluster-barrier race in FlashInfer's MNNVL fused allreduce + residual + RMSNorm kernel, which vLLM's eager `fused_allreduce_rms_norm` uses by default on single-node NVSwitch at TP≥4.

**Root cause.** Since flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3385 (still on FlashInfer main), `LamportFlags::ctaArrive()` has every thread call `__cluster_barrier_arrive()`, but only warp 0 of cluster rank 0 calls `__cluster_barrier_wait()`. Before that change it was a full `cluster.sync()`. The other CTAs then run the RMSNorm cluster reduction, which writes into peer CTAs' shared memory via `cluster.map_shared_rank`, with no guarantee the peer CTA is resident. If the timing slips, that DSMEM write lands on an absent CTA:
- Xid 13 `Graphics SM Cga Exception: CTA Not Present`
- a sticky `unspecified launch failure`

**Why this PR exposes it.** The PR queues more zero-copy host-memory gathers on the HiSparse copy stream, and now does so on spec-verify batches too. Those gathers run concurrently with the fused AR-norm, and the host reads shift CTA timing enough to hit the window. Main crashes too if you add the same gathers.

**Evidence.** I used a standalone repro with no vLLM code (below). It runs the MNNVL `allreduce_fusion` in a loop while a side stream runs a trivial kernel reading random rows of host memory. TP4, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, torch 2.14.0+cu130.

| Config | H200, driver 595.71.05 (VM) | H100, driver 580.126.09 (bare metal) |
|---|---|---|
| MNNVL, side stream on | Xid 13 within seconds | Xid 13 within seconds |
| MNNVL, two-shot / PDL off / pinned memory | Xid 13 | Xid 13 (two-shot) |
| MNNVL, side stream off | no crash | no crash |
| MNNVL, side kernel reads device memory | no crash | — |
| `trtllm` backend | no crash | — |
| **MNNVL + one-line fix (below)** | — | **no crash, one-shot and two-shot** |

`compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck` on the unpatched kernel, with no side stream, reports `Potential invalid __shared__ write ... located in a block that might not have entered yet` in `oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel`. It reports nothing on the patched kernel.

**Fix (FlashInfer).** Make every thread wait after arriving, which restores the pre-#3385 synchronization:

```diff
       __cluster_barrier_arrive();
+      __cluster_barrier_wait();

-        __cluster_barrier_wait();
```
